newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weaker against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weaker against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened further against the dollar on Friday but remained stable against the pound, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.88 against the dollar from 55.76 on Thursday, while on the pound it was posted at 92.05 from 92.03.
"The inter-bank market was very active with continued high demand from corporate importers," a commercial dealer said.
Dealers said supply was low relative to demand which led to a further weakening of the shilling. One said he did not expect the shilling to weaken further.
"You know a lot of the demand this week was from oil importers and most of it has already been met," he said. "This was a temporary situation."
"We are looking at a situation where there is no demand for dollars with small inflows of dollars now coming in and players squaring their position ahead of the weekend," the dealer said.
The local money market was tight with most banks looking. Rates were quoted at 20 percent levels from 15-20 levels.
